## Overview

RE-LY (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00262600) randomly assigned 18,113 patients with atrial fibrillation and a risk of stroke to [dabigatran](./dabigatran.md) 110 mg or 150 mg twice daily, blinded, or to unblinded adjusted-dose [warfarin](./warfarin.md), with a median follow-up of 2.0 years ([src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550.md)).

## Reported results

Rates of the primary outcome (stroke or systemic embolism) were 1.69% per year with warfarin, 1.53% per year with dabigatran 110 mg and 1.11% per year with dabigatran 150 mg. Major bleeding occurred at 3.36% per year with warfarin, 2.71% per year with 110 mg and 3.11% per year with 150 mg ([src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550.md)).

RE-LY is one of the four trials pooled in the meta-analysis of new oral anticoagulants ([src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).
